question: What does the evidence say, in time for this decision?

tricco2015.cite: Tricco et al. (2015). A scoping review of rapid review methods. BMC Medicine 13: 224.
tricco2015.checked: every quote read word for word in the Europe PMC full text (PMC4574114) on 20 Nov 2026; the article is online-only, so places are given as its sections; in-text reference numbers and figure pointers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Agree the scope
steps.text: Work with the people who must decide: agree a narrow question and the deadline, and which steps of a full systematic review will be cut.

quotes.text: Rapid reviews are a form of knowledge synthesis in which components of the systematic review process are simplified or omitted to produce information in a timely manner
four papers suggested using integrated knowledge translation, in which researchers work closely with the knowledge users to complete the rapid review
quotes.where: Results, Development papers on rapid reviews

steps.title: Narrow the search
steps.text: Search fewer sources and limit by date or language, knowing that each limit can miss studies.

quotes.text: limiting the literature search to published literature (24 %) or one database (2 %), limiting inclusion criteria by date (68 %) or language (49 %)
quotes.where: Results, streamlined methods in the 82 rapid reviews

steps.title: One screens, one checks
steps.text: Instead of two reviewers screening independently, one screens and a second checks a part of the work.

quotes.text: According to the Cochrane Collaboration, all procedures including screening citations (titles and abstracts), screening full-text articles, data abstraction, and risk of bias appraisal, should be conducted by two individuals, independently
having one person screen and another verify or screen excluded studies (6 %), having one person abstract data and another verify (23 %)
quotes.where: Results, streamlined methods in the 82 rapid reviews

steps.title: Summarise
steps.text: Most rapid reviews describe the findings in words rather than pooling them.

quotes.text: presenting results as a narrative summary (78 %)
quotes.where: Results, streamlined methods in the 82 rapid reviews

quotes.text: none suggested conducting a meta-analysis as part of the rapid review.
quotes.where: Results, Development papers on rapid reviews

steps.title: Report the shortcuts
steps.text: Say exactly which steps were cut, so readers can judge what the speed may have cost.

quotes.text: Thorough reporting of the methods is important because it is difficult to judge the bias of these reports without fully understanding what shortcuts were taken.

limits: Tricco et al. (2015) describe what rapid reviews did, not a standard for doing them; the Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group's guidance (Garritty et al. 2021) was not read for this page.
The percentages in the quotes are shares of the 82 rapid reviews Tricco et al. found that reported the step, not recommendations.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
